metadata.source: WHO ICD-11 Classification and International Clinical Practice Guidelines - Educational

references.title: WHO ICD-11: Acute Ischemic Heart Disease (BA40-BA42)
references.summary: Clinical classification and presentation criteria for acute myocardial infarction and unstable angina.
references.content: Under WHO ICD-11, Acute Myocardial Infarction (BA41) encompasses conditions characterized by myocardial necrosis in a clinical setting consistent with acute myocardial ischemia. Cardinal presentations include retrosternal chest pressure radiating to left arm or jaw, diaphoresis, dyspnea, and nausea. A normal ECG does not exclude early acute coronary syndrome.
references.source: World Health Organization (WHO) ICD-11 Mortality and Morbidity Statistics

references.title: WHO ICD-11: Cerebrovascular Diseases (8B00-8B2Z)
references.summary: Diagnostic criteria and emergency management of ischemic stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage.
references.content: WHO ICD-11 classifies acute stroke under Cerebrovascular Disease (8B11 for acute ischemic stroke, 8B00 for intracerebral hemorrhage). Time is brain: approximately 1.9 million neurons are lost per minute in untreated large vessel occlusion. Pre-hospital recognition tools such as the FAST algorithm (Face, Arm, Speech, Time) provide sensitivity exceeding 85% for anterior circulation strokes.
references.source: World Health Organization (WHO) ICD-11 / American Stroke Association Guidelines

references.title: WHO ICD-11: Acute Respiratory Infections & Asthma (CA20-CA40)
references.summary: Assessment of airway obstruction, acute hypoxemia, and asthma exacerbations.
references.content: Acute asthma exacerbations (CA23) and acute lower respiratory infections (CA40) cause progressive bronchial constriction and ventilation-perfusion mismatch. Key markers of life-threatening attack include inability to speak in sentences, silent chest on auscultation, cyanosis, and paradoxically normal or elevated PaCO2.
references.source: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) / WHO Guidelines

references.title: EAACI Anaphylaxis Management Guidelines
references.summary: Emergency clinical recognition and first-line treatment protocols for severe systemic hypersensitivity.
references.content: Anaphylaxis is a severe, life-threatening systemic hypersensitivity reaction characterized by rapid onset of airway, breathing, or circulation problems, usually associated with skin and mucosal changes. First-line pharmacotherapy is intramuscular adrenaline (epinephrine) injected into the mid-anterolateral aspect of the thigh (0.01 mg/kg, max 0.5 mg in adults). Delay in adrenaline administration is the primary risk factor for fatal outcome.
references.source: European Academy of Allergy and Clinical Immunology (EAACI)

references.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: Sepsis-3 Definitions
references.summary: Quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) and bedside sepsis recognition.
references.content: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. At the bedside or pre-hospital setting, qSOFA scores >= 2 indicate poor prognosis and potential critical deterioration: respiratory rate >= 22 breaths/min, altered mentation (GCS < 15), and systolic blood pressure <= 100 mmHg.
references.source: Society of Critical Care Medicine (SCCM) and ESICM

references.title: Emergency Severity Index (ESI) Triage Architecture
references.summary: Principles of four- and five-level acuity sorting in emergency department intake.
references.content: Triage does not establish a definitive medical diagnosis; rather, it rapidly stratifies patient acuity to ensure that critically ill patients receive immediate intervention before less acute conditions. Level 1 indicates immediate life-saving intervention needed; Level 2 represents high-risk situations, acute confusion, or severe distress; Level 3-4 denote urgent to semi-urgent routine evaluations.
references.source: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)

references.title: Canadian CT Head Rule for Minor Head Injury
references.summary: Evidence-based decision algorithm for neuroimaging following blunt head trauma.
references.content: High-risk criteria for neurosurgical intervention after head injury include: GCS score < 15 at 2 hours post-injury; suspected open or depressed skull fracture; signs of basal skull fracture (hemotympanum, raccoon eyes, Battle's sign); 2 or more episodes of vomiting; or age >= 65 years.
references.source: Lancet / Canadian Association of Emergency Physicians

references.title: MEDICARE System Scope & Clinical Limitations
references.summary: Mandatory regulatory and medical boundary declaration for computerized triage advisors.
references.content: MEDICARE is an educational navigation tool intended to guide users on when and where to seek professional medical attention. It does NOT generate clinical diagnoses, prescribe treatment, calculate validated epidemiological risk probabilities, or replace an in-person physical examination by a licensed medical practitioner. When in doubt regarding severe, worsening, or distressing symptoms, emergency medical services must be contacted without delay.

references.title: OpenStreetMap
references.summary: Open geographic map data used as a source for roads, settlements and geographic features.
references.content: OpenStreetMap (OSM) is a collaborative project providing open geographic map data used as a source for road networks, settlement landmarks, and emergency healthcare facility spatial coordinates.

references.title: OpenStreetMap Copyright and Attribution
references.summary: Data licensing, attribution and usage requirements.
references.content: Defines Open Database License (ODbL) terms, tile usage guidelines, and proper copyright attribution requirements for offline maps and extracted geographic assets.

references.title: OpenStreetMap Wiki — Downloading Data
references.summary: Documentation about obtaining geographic data for offline processing.
references.content: Official technical guidelines on downloading, extracting, and pre-processing planet dumps, regional extracts (PBF), and administrative boundary definitions for offline geographic processing.

references.title: MBTiles Specification
references.summary: Reference for the SQLite-based MBTiles format used to store map tiles.
references.content: An open specification for storing tiled map data (raster PNG/JPEG and vector PBF) inside an SQLite database container with metadata and tile schema indexed by zoom_level, tile_column, and tile_row.

references.title: Kivy Garden MapView
references.summary: Documentation for displaying interactive maps and markers in the existing Kivy application.
references.content: Interactive map display component for Kivy supporting slippy map tile layers, geographic marker placement, touch-based panning, and coordinate-to-screen projection.

references.title: SQLite Documentation
references.content: Official documentation for SQLite, the self-contained, serverless, transactional SQL engine utilized for storing patient triage records and packaging offline map tiles.

references.title: Valhalla Routing Engine
references.summary: Reference for routing algorithms and road-network navigation architecture. Candidate for evaluation, not as proof that its full engine is implemented in C.
references.content: Open-source routing engine and road-network architecture reference. Evaluated for algorithmic routing patterns and dynamic tile-based graph partitioning; MEDICARE implements a dedicated C A* routing engine for local hospital road graphs.

references.title: Android Location Permissions
references.summary: Reference for Android device location permission handling.
references.content: Android developer guidelines for runtime location permissions (ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION and ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION), privacy safeguards, and user-initiated location disclosures.

references.title: C Language Documentation
references.summary: Reference for C language functionality used in native map processing.
references.content: Standard C reference covering C11 library primitives, memory management, math functions, bit manipulation, and platform-independent data structures implemented in MEDICARE's native map engine.
